auth.reason.bad_account: the account name is not valid (DOMAIN\user or user)

state.contradicted.meaning: There is evidence in the case that contradicts the finding.
state.correlated.meaning: Several observed facts match (in time, in path or in source); correlation does not prove causation.
state.inferred.meaning: It is an inference from observed facts, not a direct observation.
state.not_assessed.meaning: No check has assessed this finding yet.
state.observed.meaning: The fact appears directly in an item of evidence in the case.
state.supported.meaning: The check found evidence in the case that supports the finding.
state.unknown.meaning: It cannot be said with the evidence in the case.
state.unproven.meaning: The evidence in the case is not enough to demonstrate it.
state.verified.meaning: The automatic check confirmed the finding against the evidence in the case (it is not an external or human review).
term.amcache.explain: The list of applications known to Windows; an entry does not prove the application ran.
term.bam.explain: Windows record of the programs each user ran and the time of the last run.
term.chain_of_custody.explain: The record of who held the evidence, when, and what was done with it, with hashes that show whether it was changed.
term.correlation.explain: Events that occur together (in time, in path or in the same source); being close does not prove that one caused the other.
term.evidence_graph.explain: The map of links between files, processes, accounts, addresses and findings; each link shows its evidence or how it was derived.
term.evtx.explain: The files in which Windows records system, security and application events.
term.ioc.explain: An item (address, domain, file, hash) associated with malicious activity; seeing it does not prove an attack on its own.
term.prefetch.explain: The traces Windows keeps when a program is started: they show which program and roughly when, not who started it.
term.provenance.explain: The source of a piece of information: the evidence item, the file (with its SHA-256 hash) and the parser that produced it.
term.sigma.explain: A rule written in a common format that searches logs for patterns of suspicious activity.
term.verification.explain: The automatic check of each finding against the evidence in the case; it is not an external or human review.
term.yara.explain: A rule that searches files or content for patterns associated with malicious programs.
why.legacy_score: Old heuristic score: {0}/100, computed from: {1}. The score is not a check and does not replace the evidence above.
why.no_limits: No limit recorded (this does not mean there is none).
why.no_reasoning: The reason for the classification is not recorded for this finding.
